front: En France, on se fait la bise pour se dire bonjour.
pronunciation: [ahn FRAHNS, ohn suh feh lah BEEZ poor suh deer bohn-ZHOOR]
back: In France, people greet each other with cheek kisses.
context: 'Faire la bise': usually two kisses, but three or four in some regions!

front: Combien de bises on se fait ici ?
pronunciation: [kohm-byan duh BEEZ ohn suh feh ee-SEE]
back: How many kisses do we do here?
context: A genuine question even among French people: it varies by region.

front: Au travail, on se serre plutôt la main.
pronunciation: [oh trah-VAHY, ohn suh sehr plü-toh lah MAN]
back: At work, people tend to shake hands.
context: 'Se serrer la main' = to shake hands.

front: On peut se tutoyer, si vous voulez.
pronunciation: [ohn puh suh tü-twah-YAY, see voo voo-LAY]
back: We can use 'tu', if you like.
context: Switching from vous to tu marks a step closer in a relationship.

front: Je n'ose pas tutoyer mon beau-père.
pronunciation: [zhuh nohz pah tü-twah-yay mohn boh-PEHR]
back: I don't dare use 'tu' with my father-in-law.
context: 'Le beau-père' = father-in-law or stepfather.

front: C'est une amie de longue date.
pronunciation: [seh tün nah-MEE duh lohng DAHT]
back: She's a long-standing friend.
context: 'De longue date' = long-standing.

front: On se connaît depuis le lycée.
pronunciation: [ohn suh koh-neh duh-pwee luh lee-SAY]
back: We've known each other since high school.
context: Present + depuis for a relationship that continues.

front: C'est plus une connaissance qu'un ami.
pronunciation: [seh plü zün koh-neh-SAHNS kan nah-MEE]
back: He's more of an acquaintance than a friend.
context: 'Une connaissance' = an acquaintance.

front: Les Français mettent du temps à se lier d'amitié.
pronunciation: [lay frahn-SEH met dü TAHN ah suh lyay dah-mee-TYAY]
back: The French take time to make friends.
context: 'Se lier d'amitié' = to become friends. Friendships form slowly but last.

front: Ils sont amis à la vie, à la mort.
pronunciation: [eel sohn tah-MEE ah lah VEE, ah lah MOR]
back: They're friends for life.
context: Literally 'to life, to death'.

front: On s'entend comme larrons en foire.
pronunciation: [ohn sahn-tahn kum lah-rohn ahn FWAHR]
back: We get along like a house on fire.
context: Idiom: like thieves at a fair.

front: Je me suis brouillé avec mon frère.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh swee broo-YAY ah-vek mohn FREHR]
back: I fell out with my brother.
context: 'Se brouiller avec' = to fall out with.

front: Ils se sont réconciliés après des années.
pronunciation: [eel suh sohn ray-kohn-see-LYAY ah-preh day zah-NAY]
back: They made up after years.
context: 'Se réconcilier' = to reconcile.

front: Il m'a posé un lapin hier soir.
pronunciation: [ee mah poh-zay an lah-PAN yehr SWAHR]
back: He stood me up last night.
context: 'Poser un lapin' (to set down a rabbit) = to stand someone up.

front: Ils sortent ensemble depuis six mois.
pronunciation: [eel sort ahn-SAHM-bluh duh-pwee see MWAH]
back: They've been going out together for six months.
context: 'Sortir ensemble' = to date.

front: Elle a craqué pour son collègue.
pronunciation: [el ah krah-kay poor sohn koh-LEG]
back: She fell for her colleague.
context: 'Craquer pour' = to fall for (informal).

front: Ils se sont mis en couple l'année dernière.
pronunciation: [eel suh sohn mee zahn KOO-pluh lah-nay dehr-NYEHR]
back: They got together last year.
context: 'Se mettre en couple' = to start a relationship.

front: Ils ont décidé de se pacser plutôt que de se marier.
pronunciation: [eel zohn day-see-day duh suh pak-SAY plü-toh kuh duh suh mah-RYAY]
back: They decided to enter a civil union rather than marry.
context: 'Le PACS' = France's civil partnership, very popular since 1999.

front: Ils vivent en concubinage.
pronunciation: [eel veev ahn kohn-kü-bee-NAHZH]
back: They live together without being married.
context: 'Le concubinage' = cohabitation (legal term). Informally: 'ils vivent ensemble'.

front: Elle a rompu avec son copain.
pronunciation: [el ah rohm-pü ah-vek sohn koh-PAN]
back: She broke up with her boyfriend.
context: 'Rompre avec' = to break up with. Informal: 'larguer quelqu'un'.

front: Il s'est fait larguer par texto.
pronunciation: [eel seh feh lar-GAY par tek-STOH]
back: He got dumped by text.
context: 'Se faire larguer' = to get dumped (informal).

front: Ils ont divorcé à l'amiable.
pronunciation: [eel zohn dee-vor-say ah lah-MYAH-bluh]
back: They divorced amicably.
context: 'À l'amiable' = amicably, by mutual agreement.

front: Mes parents sont séparés mais ils s'entendent bien.
pronunciation: [may pah-rahn sohn say-pah-RAY meh eel sahn-tahnd BYAN]
back: My parents are separated but they get along well.
context: 'S'entendre bien' = to get along.

front: C'est mon âme sœur.
pronunciation: [seh mohn nahm SUHR]
back: He's my soulmate.
context: 'L'âme sœur' = soulmate.

front: Ils filent le parfait amour.
pronunciation: [eel feel luh par-feh tah-MOOR]
back: They're living happily in love.
context: 'Filer le parfait amour' = to be blissfully in love.

front: Il est jaloux comme un tigre.
pronunciation: [ee leh zhah-loo kum an TEE-gruh]
back: He's insanely jealous.
context: Comparison idiom.

front: Elle est très pudique sur sa vie privée.
pronunciation: [el eh treh pü-DEEK sür sah vee pree-VAY]
back: She's very private about her personal life.
context: 'Pudique' = reserved, modest. French people often keep private life separate from work.

front: En France, on ne demande pas combien les gens gagnent.
pronunciation: [ahn FRAHNS, ohn nuh duh-mahnd pah kohm-byan lay zhahn GAN-yuh]
back: In France, you don't ask people how much they earn.
context: Money is a taboo topic in French conversation.

front: Arriver les mains vides chez quelqu'un, ça ne se fait pas.
pronunciation: [ah-ree-vay lay man VEED shay kel-KAN, sah nuh suh feh PAH]
back: Arriving empty-handed at someone's home just isn't done.
context: 'Ça ne se fait pas' = that's not done, it's bad manners.

front: Les Français aiment débattre, même entre amis.
pronunciation: [lay frahn-SEH em day-BAH-truh, mem ahn-truh ah-MEE]
back: French people love to debate, even among friends.
context: Disagreeing at dinner is a sign of engagement, not hostility.

front: Il ne faut pas confondre politesse et chaleur.
pronunciation: [eel nuh foh pah kohn-fohn-druh poh-lee-TES ay shah-LUHR]
back: Don't confuse politeness with warmth.
context: French politeness can seem formal before a relationship becomes warm.

front: Je me sens un peu de trop dans ce groupe.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh sahn an puh duh TROH dahn suh GROOP]
back: I feel a bit out of place in this group.
context: 'Être de trop' = to be in the way, unwanted.

front: Il a toujours le mot pour rire.
pronunciation: [ee lah too-zhoor luh moh poor REER]
back: He always knows how to make people laugh.
context: 'Avoir le mot pour rire' = to be witty.

front: C'est quelqu'un sur qui on peut compter.
pronunciation: [seh kel-kan sür kee ohn puh kohn-TAY]
back: He's someone you can count on.
context: 'Compter sur' → sur qui.

front: Elle a un caractère bien trempé.
pronunciation: [el ah an kah-rak-tehr byan trahm-PAY]
back: She has a strong personality.
context: 'Un caractère bien trempé' = strong-willed (like tempered steel).

front: Il faut savoir faire des compromis dans un couple.
pronunciation: [eel foh sah-vwahr fehr day kohm-proh-MEE dahn zan KOO-pluh]
back: You have to know how to compromise in a relationship.
context: 'Un compromis' = a compromise.

front: On a une relation fusionnelle.
pronunciation: [ohn nah ün ruh-lah-syohn fü-zyoh-NEL]
back: We have a very close, inseparable relationship.
context: 'Fusionnel' = intensely close.

front: Il a mis du temps à s'ouvrir aux autres.
pronunciation: [ee lah mee dü TAHN ah soo-vreer oh ZOH-truh]
back: It took him a while to open up to others.
context: 'S'ouvrir à' = to open up to.

front: Elle s'est fait de nouveaux amis grâce à son club de lecture.
pronunciation: [el seh feh duh noo-voh zah-MEE grahs ah sohn klüb duh lek-TÜR]
back: She made new friends thanks to her book club.
context: 'Se faire des amis' = to make friends.

front: Ils ont des points communs.
pronunciation: [eel zohn day pwan koh-MAN]
back: They have things in common.
context: 'Des points communs' = common ground.

front: Je tiens beaucoup à toi.
pronunciation: [zhuh tyan boh-koo ah TWAH]
back: You mean a lot to me.
context: 'Tenir à quelqu'un' = to care deeply about someone.

front: On s'est perdus de vue après le bac.
pronunciation: [ohn seh pehr-dü duh VÜ ah-preh luh BAK]
back: We lost touch after the baccalaureate.
context: 'Se perdre de vue' = to lose touch. 'Le bac' = the high school final exam.

front: On a repris contact grâce aux réseaux sociaux.
pronunciation: [ohn nah ruh-pree kohn-TAKT grahs oh ray-zoh soh-SYOH]
back: We got back in touch through social media.
context: 'Reprendre contact' = to get back in touch.

front: Il ne faut pas s'immiscer dans la vie des autres.
pronunciation: [eel nuh foh pah see-mee-say dahn lah vee day ZOH-truh]
back: You shouldn't meddle in other people's lives.
context: 'S'immiscer dans' = to interfere in.

front: Les absents ont toujours tort.
pronunciation: [lay zap-SAHN ohn too-zhoor TOR]
back: The absent are always in the wrong.
context: Proverb: people who aren't there get the blame.
